title: Soft-pin session affinity and data residency playbook
summary: Design notes and operator playbook for a ‘soft-pin’ regional residency strategy that provides session affinity (temporary locality) without strict tenant pinning. Goal: improve latency and cache hit-rate for multi-tenant / bursty workloads while minimizing compliance friction and migration complexity.
body:
Background:
- Problem: some customers need improved locality for short-lived conversational sessions (lower latency, higher KV cache effectiveness) but do not require strict legal region pinning for long-term storage.
- Hard pins (tenant-level region locks) are operationally heavy: contract negotiation, migration, audit bundles. We need an intermediate mechanism: soft-pin session affinity.

Goals and constraints:
- Provide per-session locality guarantees for the duration of an active session or short TTL (e.g., 30m–6h) to keep latency and KV cache benefits.
- Avoid creating long-lived attestable residency commitments (no new legal obligations).
- Ensure telemetry and audit evidence exists for troubleshooting and compliance requests (show where requests were served, session TTLs, and fallback events).
- Keep operational complexity low for oncall and SRE teams; clear operator commands to evict or migrate active sessions.
- Comply with jurisdictional rules: sensitive customer requests (explicitly tagged) must still follow hard-pin flows.

Soft-pin policy proposal (high level):
1) Session creation:
   - When a session starts, route it by default to the nearest region according to routing policy (geo + cost + tier).
   - Annotate the session with a soft-pin token: {region, started_at, ttl_seconds, policy_version, sensitivity_flag}.
2) TTL and refresh:
   - Default TTL: 45 minutes. Configurable per-application via API flag (min 5m, max 6h).
   - Activity that touches the model KV cache or is marked as "sticky" extends TTL by a bounded renewal (e.g., +15m, up to max_ttl).
3) Affinity enforcement:
   - Router will prefer the pinned region while TTL valid. If the pinned region is degraded / overloaded, route fallback to compatible region and record event (soft-pin-fallback).
4) Data handling:
   - No long-term persistent storage of user data in pinned region solely due to soft-pin. KV/cache entries are ephemeral; any persistent artifacts must follow tenant-level residency rules.
5) Sensitivity flag:
   - API or policy can mark a session as SENSITIVE. If set, treat as an override: escalate to hard-pin flow or force routing to a compliant region per customer contract.

Operator playbook (oncall + runbook snippets):
- Quick checks:
  - Inspect session list: /ops/sessions?region=eu-west1&status=active — look for soft_pin token fields.
  - If high error rate in a region: query soft-pin-fallback events and percent of active sessions pinned to that region.
- Eviction/migrate command patterns:
  - evict-session --session-id=... --reason="region-maintenance" (evict gracefully, flush KV cache to fallback store if necessary)
  - migrate-session --session-id=... --target-region=us-west1 (best-effort, invalidate local kv, set new soft_pin token).
- Postmortem traces to collect:
  - routing-decision logs, soft-pin token age, fallback reason codes, KV cache hit rate, latency percentiles pre/post migration.

Telemetry and metrics (recommended):
- Metrics to emit per session: soft_pin_region, soft_pin_ttl_remaining_seconds, renew_count, sensitivity_flag.
- Events: soft_pin_assigned, soft_pin_renewed, soft_pin_fallback, soft_pin_evicted, soft_pin_migrated.
- SLOs to monitor: percent of session requests served from pinned region while TTL valid (>90%), fallback rate (<2% under normal load), KV-hit uplift vs no-soft-pin baseline.

Fallback and audit evidence model:
- For every request, generate a compact routing header: rgn=<region>;soft_pin=<y|n>;pin_age=<s>;fallback=<none|reason>. Store these headers in request traces and in sampling logs.
- Build a short-term audit bundle (7–30 days retention) that can produce a session-level timeline if a customer asks where their session was served. Note: do not bundle persistent storage artifacts unless hard-pin applies.

Privacy / legal considerations:
- This mechanism is explicitly NOT a substitute for contractual residency. Any customer with residency clauses must request hard-pin and will be excluded from soft-pin flows by default.
- In jurisdictions requiring notice for cross-border processing, ensure API surfaces include a flag to opt-out of regional fallback.
- Keep retention of soft-pin audit bundles short by default (30 days) and configurable for legal holds.

Implementation notes and heuristics (engineer-facing):
- Router changes: add soft_pin token to session metadata; prefer in-region endpoints during scheduling. Implement lightweight sticky-route cache with TTL aware eviction.
- Runtime KV: ensure cache entries have region tags and are revocable; add quick invalidation hooks on migrate/evict.
- Telemetry: sample 1% of requests for full trace, but emit aggregate counters at 1min resolution for dashboards.
- DBs: do NOT persist session payloads due to soft-pin; store only metadata tokens and audit indices (region, timestamps, flags).

Rollout plan (canary -> gradual -> global):
- Phase 0: internal dogfood in eng teams, 1 region pair (us-west1 <-> us-east1), inject fault tests.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for selected customers (label: beta-softpin). Monitor KV hit uplift and fallback events.
- Phase 2: enable for all hosted API customers without residency contracts; default-on but opt-out via tenant flag.
- Phase 3: enable in Dedicated as an admin-configurable capability (customer chooses).

Customer communication snippets (support template):
- Q: What is soft-pin?
  - A: Soft-pin provides temporary session-level locality to lower latency and improve cache performance. It is not a legal residency guarantee — if you need that, request a region pin through our onboarding flows.
- Q: Can soft-pin move my data across borders?
  - A: Only ephemeral cached state may be served from other regions for the session duration. We don’t persist customer data to new regions as part of soft-pin.

Open questions & decisions to make:
- Maximum default TTL: 45m vs 90m? Tradeoff: longer TTL increases cache benefit but complicates evidence timelines.
- Renew policy: should any activity extend TTL or only KV-touching requests?
- Audit retention defaults: 30d vs 7d for privacy-sensitive customers.
- Operator UX: single-page session dashboard vs CLI-first approach.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [ ] Create RFC for router + KV changes (owner: Samir) — target: 2025-07-15.
- [ ] Prototype telemetry pipeline for soft_pin events (owner: Priya) — target: 2025-07-30.
- [ ] Draft customer beta invite and support script (owner: Aisha) — target: 2025-07-20.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could combine with cheap per-session encryption keys tied to region to reduce cross-border audit friction.
- Consider UI flag in Console: "session affinity" with clear legal checkbox.
- Keep language in SLA and docs explicit: soft-pin = performance optimization, not residency.

References and related docs:
- link:CONF-REGION-PIN-PRINCIPLES (hard-pin spec)
- PD-2981 (migration tooling backlog)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/734 (sticky-routing prototype)

End of draft playbook.

-- Aisha
